description: We are Qalyubia Falcons from Egypt! We love space, storytelling and coding. Our project is a website + video about the stories of things left in space, like Opportunity rover on Mars, the flag and the lunar rover on the Moon. They are not trash, they are heroes. We are looking for teammates who love design, video and web development. Let's make space stories unforgettable!
summary:
Project Qalyubia Falcons - Ghost Explorers is an interactive website created by team Qalyubia Falcons to make space exploration fun and easy for everyone. Our website allows users to explore planets, learn about exoplanets, and discover space in a simple and exciting way.

We used real NASA data from NASA Eyes on the Solar System, NASA Open Data Portal, and NASA Exoplanet Archive to provide accurate scientific information. The website was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and hosted on Netlify.

Our goal is to inspire young people in Egypt and around the world to love science and space. By turning complex space data into a visual and interactive experience, we help students, kids, and space lovers understand the universe better and dream bigger.
details:
Ghost Explorers is an interactive educational website that helps users explore planets, exoplanets, and space missions in a fun and simple way.

What we developed:

- A homepage that introduces the universe and our mission

- An Explore Planets section with real information about each planet

- An Exoplanets section using NASA Exoplanet Archive data

- A fun quiz and interactive design for kids and students

How it addresses the challenge:

Our project turns complex NASA space data into easy, visual, and interactive content that anyone can understand, even without a science background.

Benefits and impact:

It makes learning about space exciting, helps students in schools, and encourages young people in Egypt and worldwide to be interested in science, technology, and space exploration.

Software used:

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the website, Canva for design, and Netlify for hosting. We used NASA Eyes on the Solar System, NASA Open Data Portal, and NASA Exoplanet Archive for real data. Tanks for listen
